bc_tourista.blurb: Tourista is a small boulder cluster in the Bealby Road bouldering zone on the edge of Nelson, in the West Kootenay. It has five problems, running from an easy warm-up grade up to the V6 range, with a spread that suits a mixed group for a short session. The problems lean on arete lines, sidepulls and slopey rails, and one steep bulge holds a hard low-start line. The boulders sit only a few metres above the road, so the walk is trivial and a pad plus a spotter is all you need. It pairs well with neighbouring sectors in the same zone.

bc_split_pea.blurb: Split Pea is a compact bouldering sector within the Bealby Road zone near Nelson, in the West Kootenay of British Columbia. It holds five problems that spread from low V-grades to the V8 range, with two in the V7 band, so it leans toward stronger boulderers rather than beginners. It is best treated as an add-on to the other sectors close by in the same zone.

bc_the_spirit.blurb: The Spirit is one large free-standing boulder next to the forest road in the Ladybird Creek bouldering zone of the West Kootenay. It carries five problems that climb from an easy V1 to the V8-V9 range, so the upper end is for strong climbers while a couple of lines suit warming up. Because it sits at the roadside it works for a quick session, or as a stop before heading to the main Ladybird concentrations. There is room for more lines on the block, and the hardest problems are still being worked.
bc_the_spirit.parking_note: Pullout beside the creek at roughly the 7 km point up the Ladybird Creek forest road from the Pass Creek Road turnoff; the boulder is a short walk back down the road.

bc_party_crasher.blurb: Party Crasher is a small cluster of boulders in the Ladybird Creek zone of the West Kootenay. A faint cairned path leaves the main trail through the Hemlock and Slide boulders and climbs to the blocks. There are five problems, from V2 to V7, with two in the V5 range and the V7 serving as the area's hardest test. It suits a short visit tacked onto a day among the larger Ladybird concentrations rather than a day of its own.

bc_the_penthouse.blurb: The Penthouse is the highest and newest section of the Ladybird Creek bouldering zone in the West Kootenay, set on a flatter bench above the main boulders. Reaching it takes a scramble through the boulders on a cairned trail, with a ladder near the top, and it is the longest walk uphill at Ladybird, roughly ten to fifteen minutes from the car. Five problems are developed here, from V0 to the V8 range, including two in the V7-V8 band, and the bench offers room for further development.

bc_galaxy_buttress.blurb: Galaxy Buttress is a prominent buttress jutting into the Cheakamus River in The Gorge, part of Cheakamus Canyon on Highway 99 between Squamish and Whistler. It has five routes, mixing sport and trad, in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, and several are multi-pitch, up to five pitches. The climbing is smooth and compact, favouring fingery edges and rails. One line follows the crest of the arete while the others take the steeper sides. The trail in crosses talus into a narrow bedrock canyon.

bc_middle_bear.blurb: Middle Bear is a light-coloured wall above Lower Bear in the Bear Country zone of KLO Creek, in the Okanagan near Kelowna. It has five sport routes in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, three of them 5.10 and two 5.11, making it a good place for climbers moving up from the low 5.10s. The wall catches morning sun, and the climbing is technical rather than steep. The approach is a forest walk of about twenty minutes from the parking area, including a creek crossing.
bc_middle_bear.approach: About twenty minutes on foot from the parking area, with a creek to cross; take care at the crossing in spring.

bc_wayback_layback_area_ftgu_right.blurb: The Wayback Layback Area is the right-hand end of the From The Ground Up wall, the lowest tier of Harrison Bluffs in the Fraser Valley. It has five trad routes, from an easy line up through the 5.10s to a 5.12 finger crack, with the main lines being crack and layback climbing. It has the shortest approach on the bluffs, around a minute from the powerline road. Early spring can leave the routes damp.
bc_wayback_layback_area_ftgu_right.approach: About one minute from the powerline road to the base.
